questions.q: Software construction is best described as a project phase situated:
o: entirely outside the software engineering lifecycle
before requirements gathering and problem definition
after system testing and before deployment
between planning (design) and quality assurance
questions.e: Construction is a phase of a project that sits in between plan (design) and quality assurance.

questions.q: Software construction is defined as the construction of working, meaningful software through a combination of coding, validation, unit testing, integration testing and:
o: procurement
contract negotiation
marketing
debugging
questions.e: Software construction is a fundamental act of software engineering: the construction of working, meaningful software through a combination of coding, validation, unit testing, integration testing and debugging.

questions.q: Software construction is linked to all other software engineering activities, but most strongly to which two?
o: Configuration management and deployment
Software design and software testing
Requirements elicitation and contract management
Cost estimation and staffing
questions.e: Construction is most strongly linked to software design and software testing, because the construction process itself involves significant design and test activity.

questions.q: In relation to the surrounding activities, software construction:
o: uses the output of design and provides one of the inputs to testing
uses the output of testing and provides one of the inputs to design
produces both the design and the test plan as its only outputs
is independent of design and testing
questions.e: Construction uses the output of design and provides one of the inputs to testing.

questions.q: How many fundamentals of software construction are identified in the standard list that includes minimizing complexity and anticipating change?
o: Seven
Five
Three
Four
questions.e: The five fundamentals are: minimizing complexity, anticipating change, reuse, constructing for verification, and standards in construction.

questions.q: Which of the following is one of the five fundamentals of software construction?
o: Constructing for verification
Deferring all testing to the customer
Outsourcing non-core modules
Maximizing lines of code per developer
questions.e: The five fundamentals are minimizing complexity, anticipating change, reuse, constructing for verification, and standards in construction.

questions.q: In software construction, reduced complexity is primarily achieved by emphasizing the creation of code that is:
o: as short as possible regardless of readability
heavily commented rather than well structured
simple and readable rather than clever
clever rather than simple
questions.e: Minimizing complexity means emphasizing code that is simple and readable rather than clever; it is accomplished through standards and specific coding techniques. As functionality increases, so does complexity.

questions.q: Anticipating change helps engineers build extensible software, which means they can:
o: rewrite the product from scratch at lower cost
enhance a product without disrupting the underlying structure
freeze the requirements permanently
remove the need for any future testing
questions.e: Extensible software can be enhanced without disrupting the underlying structure, which is the point of anticipating change.

questions.q: Research spanning 25 years found that the cost of rework can be how much more expensive than getting the requirements right the first time?
o: 100 to 1000 times, and 50 to 100 times for smaller projects
2 to 5 times, and 1 to 2 times for smaller projects
10 to 100 times, and 5 to 10 times for smaller projects
exactly 15 times regardless of project size
questions.e: The cost of rework can be 10 to 100 times more expensive than getting the requirements right the first time, dropping to 5 to 10 times for smaller projects.

questions.q: Anticipation of change affects how software is constructed in which of the following ways?
o: Licensing terms and pricing model
Hardware procurement and network topology
Choice of office location and team size only
Use of control structures, handling of errors and source code organization
questions.e: Anticipating change affects the use of control structures, handling of errors, source code organization, code documentation and coding standards.

questions.q: Constructing for verification means building software so that faults can be:
o: corrected only after release by the maintenance team
hidden from independent testers to avoid alarm
ferreted out readily by the engineers writing it and during independent testing
tolerated at runtime without being detected
questions.e: Constructing for verification means building software such that faults can be found readily by the engineers writing it as well as during independent testing and operational activities.

questions.q: Which technique supports constructing for verification?
o: Removing unit tests to reduce build time
Avoiding coding standards so developers are unconstrained
Maximizing the use of clever language idioms
Restricted use of complex or hard-to-understand language structures
questions.e: Techniques that support constructing for verification include following coding standards to support code reviews, unit testing, organizing code to support automated testing, and restricted use of complex or hard-to-understand language structures.

questions.q: Reuse has two closely related facets. Which pair is correct?
o: Construction for reuse and construction with reuse
Construction by reuse and construction against reuse
Reuse in design and reuse in testing
Internal reuse and external reuse
questions.e: Construction for reuse means creating reusable software assets; construction with reuse means reusing software assets in the construction of a new solution.

questions.q: Standards affecting construction may be external or internal. Internal standards are those created:
o: by the programming language designers
by the end users of the product
at the corporate level
by international standards organizations
questions.e: External standards are created by international organizations; internal standards are created at the corporate level.

questions.q: In the list of construction standards, diagrammatic standards for notations such as UML fall under which category?
o: Coding standards
Platforms
Tools
Communication methods
questions.e: The standards categories are communication methods, programming languages, coding standards, platforms, and tools; tools is the category that covers diagrammatic standards for notations like UML.

questions.q: Which category of construction standards covers standards for document formats and contents?
o: Programming languages
Communication methods
Tools
Platforms
questions.e: Communication methods covers standards such as those for document formats and contents.

questions.q: Which statement explains why construction's product is so significant?
o: The source code is often the only accurate description of the software
The source code is normally discarded after delivery
The source code is the least accurate description of the software
The source code is produced only for very large projects
questions.e: Construction's product, the source code, is often the only accurate description of the software.

questions.q: Among the reasons software construction matters, which activity is described as the only one guaranteed to be done?
o: Requirements development
Architecture
Corrective maintenance
Construction
questions.e: Construction is the only activity that is guaranteed to be done; it is also a large part of, and the central activity in, software development.

questions.q: In the list of software development activities, which activity immediately follows software architecture (high-level design)?
o: Detailed design
Coding and debugging
Construction planning
Unit testing
questions.e: The ordered list runs: problem definition, requirements development, construction planning, software architecture or high-level design, detailed design, coding and debugging, unit testing, integration testing, integration, system testing, corrective maintenance.

questions.q: Which of the following is a software construction activity?
o: Tuning code to make it smaller and faster
Negotiating the project budget with the client
Preparing the marketing launch plan
Recruiting and interviewing new developers
questions.e: Construction activities include verifying the groundwork, determining how code will be tested, designing and writing classes and routines, creating and naming variables and constants, selecting control structures, unit and integration testing and debugging, peer review of low-level designs and code, polishing code through formatting and commenting, integrating separately created components, and tuning code to make it smaller and faster.

questions.q: A math tutor program whose loop never terminates regardless of whether the answer is correct, has no error processing for nonnumeric input, and repeats the same problem indefinitely, illustrates which general conclusion?
o: Error processing should always be added after release
The failure to design intentionally often yields narrowly scoped and brittle software
Designing intentionally slows development with no quality benefit
Looping constructs should be avoided in educational software
questions.e: The deficiencies in that example illustrate that the failure to design intentionally often yields narrowly scoped and brittle software.

questions.q: At minimum, a designer should determine which four things?
o: Database vendor, server count, bandwidth, and storage
Team size, schedule, budget, and office layout
Required domain knowledge, form and bounds of input, error processing, and output
Programming language, IDE, compiler version, and build tool
questions.e: Minimally, a designer should determine required domain knowledge, the form and bounds of input, error processing, and output.

questions.q: Which book is 'A Practical Handbook of Software Construction'?
o: Objects First with Java by Barnes and Kolling
Object-Oriented Software Construction by Bertrand Meyer
Code Complete by Steve McConnell
Software Essentials: Design and Construction by Adair Dingle
questions.e: Code Complete: A Practical Handbook of Software Construction is by Steve McConnell. Objects First with Java: A Practical Introduction Using BlueJ is by David J. Barnes and Michael Kolling.

questions.q: Which chapter of SWEBOK V3 (2014) deals with software construction?
o: Chapter 12
Chapter 24
Chapter 3
Chapter 1
questions.e: SWEBOK V3, 2014, chapter 3 covers software construction.

questions.q: Object-Oriented Software Construction, second edition, was written by:
o: Gerardus Blokdyk
Bertrand Meyer
Steve McConnell
Adair Dingle
questions.e: Object-Oriented Software Construction, second edition, is by Bertrand Meyer; Software Construction: A Complete Guide (2020) is by Gerardus Blokdyk; Software Essentials: Design and Construction (3rd edition, 2014) is by Adair Dingle.

questions.q: Why is excessive and overlapping information identified as a problem in modern software?
o: It reduces the size of the compiled binary
It can be disorienting and the required details can be distracting
It always increases execution speed
It eliminates the need for a user interface
questions.e: Excessive and overlapping information can be disorienting, and the required details can be distracting.

questions.q: Construction can account for as much as what proportion of total project costs?
o: 40 percent
25 percent
90 percent
65 percent
questions.e: The construction part of software development can account for as much as 65 percent of the total project costs, which is why the 'measure twice, cut once' metaphor applies.

questions.q: The metaphor 'measure twice, cut once' is used to make which point about software projects?
o: Every requirement must be reviewed by exactly two people
Code should always be written twice and the better version kept
Testing should be performed twice before release
Much of the success or failure is determined before construction begins, so preparation matters
questions.e: As with building construction, much of the success or failure of the project has already been determined before construction begins, so good preparation is essential.

questions.q: High-quality practices used by programmers who build high-quality software emphasize quality:
o: only in the middle, during coding
only at the beginning, during requirements
only at the end, during acceptance testing
at the beginning, the middle and the end of a project
questions.e: Such practices emphasize quality at the beginning, quality at the middle and quality at the end of a project. Paying attention to quality is also the best way to improve productivity.

questions.q: Paying attention to quality is described as the best way to improve:
o: productivity
team morale
customer pricing
hardware utilization
questions.e: Paying attention to quality is also the best way to improve productivity.

questions.q: Evidence about whether upstream activities such as architecture, design and planning are useful shows that:
o: data since the 1990s shows preparation has no measurable effect
preparation has only ever been studied theoretically
preparation helps only on projects of fewer than ten people
data from the 1970s to the present day indicates projects run best if appropriate preparation is done before construction
questions.e: Data from the 1970s to the present day clearly indicates that projects will run best if appropriate preparation activities are done before construction begins in earnest.

questions.q: The overarching goal of preparation is:
o: staff utilization
risk reduction
documentation volume
language selection
questions.e: The overarching goal of preparation is risk reduction: a good project planner clears major risks out of the way as early as possible.

questions.q: Which are the most common project risks in software development?
o: Hardware failure and network latency
Compiler bugs and library incompatibility
Staff turnover and office relocation
Poor requirements and poor project planning
questions.e: The most common project risks in software development are poor requirements and poor project planning.

questions.q: Which of the following is a cause of incomplete preparation?
o: Preparation requires a formal mathematical proof
Preparation tools are prohibitively expensive
Managers are notoriously unsympathetic to programmers who spend time on construction prerequisites
Preparation is forbidden by most coding standards
questions.e: The causes given are: developers assigned to upstream activities lack the expertise; some programmers know how but cannot resist the urge to begin coding as soon as possible; and managers are notoriously unsympathetic to programmers who spend time on construction prerequisites.

questions.q: If an architecture defect costs $1000 to fix while the architecture is being created, what is the quoted cost of fixing it during system test?
questions.e: An architecture defect that costs $1000 to fix when the architecture is being created can cost $15,000 to fix during system test, a factor of fifteen.

questions.q: A well-run project devotes approximately what share of its effort to requirements, architecture and up-front planning?
o: 10 to 20 percent of effort
40 to 50 percent of effort
20 to 30 percent of effort
2 to 5 percent of effort
questions.e: A well-run project devotes about 10 to 20 percent of its effort and about 20 to 30 percent of its schedule to requirements, architecture and up-front planning.

questions.q: A well-run project devotes approximately what share of its schedule to requirements, architecture and up-front planning?
o: 20 to 30 percent of schedule
50 to 60 percent of schedule
10 to 20 percent of schedule
5 to 10 percent of schedule
questions.e: About 10 to 20 percent of effort and about 20 to 30 percent of the schedule go to requirements, architecture and up-front planning.

questions.q: According to the Cocomo II estimation model, programmers working in a language they have used for three years or more are about how much more productive than equally experienced programmers new to that language?
o: 30 percent more productive
10 percent more productive
twice as productive
3 times more productive
questions.e: Cocomo II data shows about 30 percent higher productivity for programmers with three or more years in a language. A separate, earlier IBM study found programmers with extensive language experience were more than three times as productive as those with minimal experience.

questions.q: An earlier study at IBM found that programmers with extensive experience in a programming language were:
o: about 30 percent more productive than those with minimal experience
equally productive once a project exceeded six months
less productive because of entrenched habits
more than three times as productive as those with minimal experience
questions.e: The IBM study found more than a threefold productivity difference; the Cocomo II figure of about 30 percent refers to three or more years of experience in the language.

questions.q: Software design is defined as the conception, invention or contrivance of a scheme for:
o: turning a specification for a computer program into an operational program
estimating the cost and schedule of a program
selecting the hardware on which a program will run
turning an operational program into a formal specification
questions.e: The phrase 'software design' means the conception, invention, or contrivance of a scheme for turning a specification for a computer program into an operational program.

questions.q: Design is described as the activity that links:
o: requirements to coding and debugging
testing to deployment
budgeting to staffing
maintenance to retirement
questions.e: Design is the activity that links requirements to coding and debugging. A good top-level design provides a structure that can safely contain multiple lower-level designs.

questions.q: A good top-level design is valuable because it:
o: removes the need for any lower-level design
fixes the implementation language permanently
provides a structure that can safely contain multiple lower-level designs
guarantees the absence of defects
questions.e: A good top-level design provides a structure that can safely contain multiple lower level designs. Good design is useful on small projects and indispensable on large projects.

questions.q: The design challenge of non-determinism refers to the fact that:
o: three designers may produce three different but acceptable designs
design outcomes cannot be evaluated at all
random number generators are needed during design
designs always converge on a single optimum
questions.e: Non-determinism asks what the outcome should be: three designers may produce three different but acceptable designs. Other challenges are sloppiness (knowing when a design is good enough) and the fact that the process is heuristic rather than an algorithm.

questions.q: The design process is characterised as:
o: an algorithm with provable termination
heuristic, not an algorithm
a fully automatable compilation step
a purely clerical transcription task
questions.e: The process is heuristic, not an algorithm: it consists of things to try that sometimes work. Dogmatic adherence to any single methodology hurts creativity and hurts programs.

questions.q: Which pair of desirable design characteristics is correctly stated?
o: High fan-in and high fan-out
Low fan-in and low fan-out only
Low fan-in and high fan-out
High fan-in and low to medium fan-out
questions.e: The desirable characteristics listed are minimal complexity, ease of maintenance, minimal connectedness, extensibility, reusability, high fan-in, low to medium fan-out, portability, leanness and stratification.

questions.q: Which of the following is one of the listed desirable characteristics of a good design?
o: Maximal connectedness
Minimal connectedness
High fan-out
Maximal complexity
questions.e: Minimal connectedness is among the desirable characteristics; the list also includes minimal complexity, ease of maintenance, extensibility, reusability, high fan-in, low to medium fan-out, portability, leanness and stratification.

questions.q: Software's Primary Technical Imperative is:
o: minimizing memory footprint
maximizing execution speed
maximizing code volume
managing complexity
questions.e: Software's Primary Technical Imperative is managing complexity, greatly aided by a design focus on simplicity.

questions.q: Simplicity in design is achieved in two general ways. Which pair is correct?
o: Minimizing the number of files, and maximizing comment density
Deferring all design to construction, and avoiding notation
Minimizing essential complexity the brain must handle at one time, and keeping accidental complexity from proliferating needlessly
Removing all abstraction, and writing shorter identifiers
questions.e: Simplicity is achieved by minimizing the amount of essential complexity that anyone's brain has to deal with at any one time, and by keeping accidental complexity from proliferating needlessly.

questions.q: Which statement about good design is correct?
o: Good design requires dogmatic adherence to one methodology
Good design makes creativity unnecessary
Good design is achieved in a single pass if the methodology is followed strictly
Good design is iterative: the more design possibilities tried, the better the final design
questions.e: Good design is iterative; the more design possibilities you try, the better your final design will be. Dogmatic adherence to any single methodology hurts creativity and hurts programs.

questions.q: Studies of programming-language choice have shown that programmers are more productive:
o: using whichever language is newest
using a language with the fewest keywords
using a familiar language than an unfamiliar one
only when the language is statically typed
questions.e: Programming-language choice affects productivity and code quality in several ways; programmers are more productive using a familiar language than an unfamiliar one.

questions.q: The inner contents of a Java class consist of:
o: fields, constructors and methods
headers, bodies and signatures
packages, imports and comments
variables, loops and conditionals
questions.e: A class body contains fields, constructors and methods, wrapped by the outer class declaration.

questions.q: Fields are also known as:
o: instance variables
return values
local variables
parameters
questions.e: Fields store values for an object, are also known as instance variables, and define the state of an object.

questions.q: In the declaration 'private int price;' the three elements in order are:
o: visibility modifier, type, variable name
visibility modifier, variable name, type
type, visibility modifier, variable name
variable name, type, visibility modifier
questions.e: 'private' is the visibility modifier, 'int' is the type and 'price' is the variable name.

questions.q: Words such as public, class, private and int, which have a special meaning in the language, are known as:
o: literals, also called constants
identifiers, also called labels
keywords, also called reserved words
operators, also called delimiters
questions.e: Words with a special meaning in the language, such as public, class, private and int, are keywords, also known as reserved words.

questions.q: Which statement about constructors is correct?
o: They have the same name as their class and store initial values into the fields
They must be declared private so that objects cannot be created externally
They are optional only in classes that have no methods
They have the same name as the first field and return that field
questions.e: Constructors initialize an object, have the same name as their class, are closely associated with the fields, store initial values into the fields, and may take external parameter values for this purpose.

questions.q: An assignment statement has the general form:
o: variable == expression;
expression = variable;
variable = expression;
variable := expression;
questions.e: Values are stored into fields and other variables via assignment statements of the form variable = expression; for example price = cost;.

questions.q: When a new value is assigned to a variable:
o: the assignment fails unless the variable was first cleared
both the old and new values are retained in a history
the old value is moved to the next memory slot
any previous value is lost, because a variable stores a single value
questions.e: A variable stores a single value, so any previous value is lost on assignment.

questions.q: Which of the following is a poor choice of variable name?
o: amount
t5
age
price
questions.e: Expressive names such as price, amount, name and age make code easier to understand; single-letter or cryptic names such as w, t5 and xyz123 should be avoided.

questions.q: A method's header provides its:
o: signature
visibility only
body
return statement
questions.e: The header provides the method's signature, such as 'public int getPrice()'; the body encloses the method's statements.

questions.q: Which of the following does a method header NOT tell us?
o: The number of statements inside the method body
What parameters it takes
The name of the method
Whether it returns a result
questions.e: The header tells us the name of the method, what parameters it takes, whether it returns a result, and its visibility to objects of other classes. The number of statements is a property of the body.

questions.q: Which statement about accessor methods is correct?
o: An accessor method must take at least one parameter
An accessor method always has a void return type and prints the value
An accessor method always has a return type that is not void and contains a return statement
An accessor method alters the state of the object it is called on
questions.e: An accessor method provides information about an object: its return type is not void, it returns a value of the type given in the header, and it contains a return statement. Returning is not printing.

questions.q: 'Returning is not printing' is emphasised because:
o: printed values cannot be stored in fields
a return statement passes a value back to the caller rather than displaying it
printing is faster than returning
a method cannot contain both a print and a return
questions.e: An accessor returns a value (a result) to its caller; printing displays text but does not hand a value back, so the two are not interchangeable.

questions.q: Mutator methods change an object's state by:
o: returning a value of non-void type to the caller
declaring new fields at runtime
changing the value of one or more fields, typically using assignment statements
creating a new object each time they are called
questions.e: Mutator methods have a header and a body, mutate the object's state by changing the value of one or more fields, typically contain assignment statements, and often receive parameters.

questions.q: A typical 'set' mutator method has which distinctive form?
o: non-void return type, one parameter, and no body
void return type, two parameters of differing types, and a loop
void return type, a name related to the field, a single parameter of the field's type, and a single assignment statement
non-void return type, no parameters, and a single return statement
questions.e: A set mutator has a void return type, a method name related to the field name, a single parameter with the same type as the field, and a single assignment statement.

questions.q: Given the method 'public void setDiscount(int amount) { discount = amount; }', what can be inferred about discount?
o: It is a field of type int
It is a constructor parameter only
It is a parameter of type int
It is a local variable of type int
questions.e: Because the method assigns the int parameter to discount and discount is not declared locally, discount must be a field of type int, that is 'private int discount;'.

questions.q: Protective mutators protect fields because:
o: they make the field public so it can be validated externally
they prevent the field from ever being changed
they copy the field into a local variable before returning it
the parameter may be checked for validity and rejected if inappropriate rather than simply assigned
questions.e: A set method does not have to assign the parameter to the field: the parameter may be checked for validity and rejected if inappropriate. Mutators thereby protect fields and support encapsulation.

questions.q: In Java, what is the result of the expression "wind" + "ow"?
o: a compile error
"wind ow"
"ow" overwrites "wind"
"window"
questions.e: The + operator is overloaded: applied to two strings it concatenates them, giving "window". Applied to two numbers it adds them, so 4 + 5 gives 9.

questions.q: What does the expression "Result: " + 6 produce?
o: "Result: 6"
a compile error
"Result: " only
questions.e: When one operand is a String, + concatenates, converting the number to text, so the result is the string "Result: 6".

questions.q: What does System.out.println(5 + 6 + "hello"); print?
o: 56hello
hello56
hello11
11hello
questions.e: Evaluation is left to right: 5 + 6 is numeric addition giving 11, then 11 + "hello" concatenates, so 11hello is printed.

questions.q: What does System.out.println("hello" + 5 + 6); print?
o: 56hello
11hello
hello56
hello11
questions.e: Evaluation is left to right: "hello" + 5 concatenates to "hello5", then + 6 concatenates again, giving hello56. The contrasting case 5 + 6 + "hello" prints 11hello.

questions.q: Which conditional statement correctly rejects a non-positive amount in a money-insertion method?
o: if(balance > 0) { amount = amount + balance; } else { print a warning }
if(amount > 0) { print a warning } else { balance = balance + amount; }
if(amount = 0) { balance = balance + amount; } else { print a warning }
if(amount > 0) { balance = balance + amount; } else { print a warning }
questions.e: The test must guard the update: when amount is greater than zero the balance is increased, otherwise a message asking for a positive amount is printed.

questions.q: Which of these is true of parameters?
o: They are accessible throughout the whole class
The method itself sets their values rather than receiving them
They persist for the lifetime of the object
They receive values from outside the method and each call receives a fresh set of values
questions.e: Parameters receive values from outside the method, help it complete its task, get a fresh set of values on each call, and are short lived. Fields, by contrast, persist for the life of an object and are accessible throughout the class.

questions.q: Which statement distinguishes local variables from parameters?
o: Local variables persist for the lifetime of the object, parameters do not
A local variable receives an external value, whereas a parameter is set by the method
The method sets a local variable's value, whereas a parameter receives an external value
Local variables require a visibility modifier, parameters do not
questions.e: Both are short lived, but a method sets the values of its own local variables; unlike parameters they do not receive external values. Local variables are used for temporary calculation and storage, exist only while the method executes, and are accessible only within the method.

questions.q: A local variable declaration differs visibly from a field declaration in that it has:
o: no type
no visibility modifier
no semicolon
no name
questions.e: In a method such as 'public int refundBalance() { int amountToRefund; ... }', the local variable amountToRefund is declared with a type and name but no visibility modifier.

questions.q: What is the scope of a local variable?
o: All methods of the same class
The block in which it is declared
The lifetime of the containing object
The whole class in which it appears
questions.e: The scope of a local variable is the block in which it is declared; the scope of a field is its whole class.

questions.q: What is the lifetime of a field?
o: The lifetime of its containing object
The time of execution of the block in which it is declared
A single method call
Until the first assignment to it
questions.e: The lifetime of a field is the lifetime of its containing object; the lifetime of a local variable is the time of execution of the block in which it is declared.

questions.q: Which statement about scope and lifetime is correct?
o: Both scope and lifetime are runtime properties
Scope is static (textual) while lifetime is dynamic (runtime)
Scope is dynamic (runtime) while lifetime is static (textual)
Both scope and lifetime are static properties
questions.e: Each block defines a new scope and scopes may be nested; scope is static, meaning textual, while lifetime is dynamic, meaning determined at runtime.

questions.q: Which three kinds of block each define a new scope?
o: Constructor, field and parameter
Class, method and statement
Package, class and field
File, import and class
questions.e: Each block defines a new scope: class, method and statement blocks. Scopes may be nested, for instance a statement block inside another block inside a method body inside a class body.

questions.q: A ticket machine class that can issue tickets of several different values, compared with one fixed price, is:
o: impossible to express in an object-oriented language
identical in complexity because price is just a field
simpler to program because one class replaces several
significantly more complicated to program, though multiple instances with different prices are easy to create
questions.e: It is significantly more complicated to program a class to issue tickets of different values than to have a single price; however, with object-oriented programming it is easy to create multiple instances of the class, each with its own price setting.

questions.q: The behaviour of the simple ticket machine is inadequate in which respects?
o: No keywords and no visibility modifiers
No fields, no constructors, and no methods
No print output and no return values
No checks on the amounts entered, no refunds, and no checks for a sensible initialization
questions.e: Its shortcomings are that there are no checks on the amounts entered, no refunds, and no checks for a sensible initialization.

questions.q: Abstraction is defined as the ability to:
o: divide a whole into well-defined parts that can be built separately
ignore details of parts in order to focus attention on a higher level of a problem
hide a field behind an accessor method
replace an object reference with a primitive value
questions.e: Abstraction is the ability to ignore details of parts to focus attention on a higher level of a problem. Modularisation is the separate idea of dividing a whole into well-defined parts.

questions.q: Modularisation is defined as the process of dividing a whole into well-defined parts that:
o: interact only through public fields
cannot be examined independently once assembled
can be built and examined separately and which interact in well-defined ways
share all of their fields and methods with one another
questions.e: Modularisation is the process of dividing a whole into well-defined parts, which can be built and examined separately, and which interact in well-defined ways.

questions.q: A clock display built from two two-digit displays rather than one four-digit display is an example of:
o: polymorphism
modularisation
inheritance
overloading
questions.e: Splitting the clock display into two two-digit displays plus some glue code to join them is an application of modularisation.

questions.q: In a NumberDisplay class with fields limit and value, which increment method correctly makes the value roll over?
o: value = (value % limit) + 1;
value = value + 1 - limit;
value = (value + 1) / limit;
value = (value + 1) % limit;
questions.e: Taking the remainder after incrementing makes the value wrap back to 0 once it reaches the limit: value = (value + 1) % limit.

questions.q: In Java, what is the value of 17 / 5?
questions.e: The division operator applied to int operands returns the integer result of an integer division, so 17 / 5 is 3. The modulo operator returns the remainder, so 17 % 5 is 2.

questions.q: In Java, what is the value of 17 % 5?
questions.e: The modulo operator (%) returns the integer remainder of an integer division: 17 % 5 is 2, while 17 / 5 is 3.

questions.q: A getDisplayValue method returns "0" + value when value is less than 10 and "" + value otherwise. What is its purpose?
o: To convert the value from a String to an int
To round the value up to the nearest ten
To reset the value to zero when it is small
To pad single-digit values with a leading zero so the display is always two characters
questions.e: Prefixing "0" for values below ten gives a two-character result such as 07, while concatenating with the empty string converts larger values to text unchanged.

questions.q: In a ClockDisplay class, which constructor body correctly creates a 24-hour and a 60-minute display?
o: hours = new ClockDisplay(24); minutes = new ClockDisplay(60);
hours = new NumberDisplay(24); minutes = new NumberDisplay(60);
hours = new NumberDisplay(60); minutes = new NumberDisplay(24);
hours = new NumberDisplay(23); minutes = new NumberDisplay(59);
questions.e: The roll-over limits are the counts, not the maximum values, so the hours display is created with 24 and the minutes display with 60.

questions.q: A timeTick method advances the clock by one minute. Which logic is correct?
o: hours.increment(); if(hours.getValue() == 0) { minutes.increment(); } updateDisplay();
minutes.increment(); hours.increment(); updateDisplay();
minutes.increment(); if(minutes.getValue() == 0) { hours.increment(); } updateDisplay();
minutes.increment(); if(minutes.getValue() == 60) { hours.increment(); } updateDisplay();
questions.e: The minutes are incremented first; because the minute display rolls over to 0 at its limit, a value of 0 signals that the hour must also be incremented. The display string is then refreshed.

questions.q: Which statement correctly builds a display string of the form hh:mm from two NumberDisplay fields?
o: displayString = hours.getDisplayValue() + ":" + minutes.getDisplayValue();
displayString = hours + ":" + minutes;
displayString = hours.getValue() + minutes.getValue();
displayString = ":" + hours.getDisplayValue() + minutes.getDisplayValue();
questions.e: The two-character display values are fetched from each NumberDisplay and joined with a colon by string concatenation.

questions.q: Consider: int a; int b; a = 42; b = a; a = a + 1; Has b changed?
o: Yes, because both are declared in the same statement
No, because b holds a copy of the primitive value
No, because b was never assigned
Yes, because b refers to the same storage as a
questions.e: For primitive types the assignment b = a copies the value, so later changing a leaves b at 42. For object types, by contrast, the assignment copies a reference and both variables then refer to the same object.

questions.q: Consider: Person a; Person b; a = new Person("Everett"); b = a; a.changeName("Delmar"); Does b.getName() now show the new name?
o: No, because b holds an independent copy of the object
No, because changeName affects only local state
Yes, because a and b refer to the same object
Yes, but only after b is reassigned
questions.e: For object types the assignment b = a copies the reference, not the object, so both variables refer to the same Person and a change made through a is visible through b.

questions.q: In a class diagram, an arrow from ClockDisplay to NumberDisplay means that ClockDisplay contains a reference to a NumberDisplay object through:
o: a field only
a field, a method parameter or a method local variable
an inheritance relationship
a constructor parameter only
questions.e: A class diagram arrow of this kind means the class contains a reference, either through a field, a method parameter or a method local variable, to an object of the other class. The object diagram is more specific.

questions.q: What does the object diagram for a ClockDisplay show that its class diagram does not?
o: That NumberDisplay has no fields
That NumberDisplay inherits from ClockDisplay
That it holds two references, each a field, to a NumberDisplay
That the reference is a local variable
questions.e: The class diagram shows only that a reference exists; the object diagram shows that ClockDisplay actually contains two references, each of which is a field, to a NumberDisplay.

questions.q: In the call 'hours = new NumberDisplay(24);' against a constructor declared 'public NumberDisplay(int rollOver)', the value 24 is:
o: the formal parameter, matched to the supplied argument rollOver
a field of class ClockDisplay
a local variable of the calling method
the supplied argument, matched to the formal parameter rollOver
questions.e: rollOver in the constructor header is the formal parameter; 24 at the call site is the supplied argument.

questions.q: Which form is used to call a method on another object?
o: this.methodName(argument, list)
objectName.methodName(argument, list)
ClassName::methodName(argument, list)
methodName(argument, list)
questions.e: An external call takes the form objectName.methodName(arguments). An internal call on the object's own class omits the object name, or optionally uses this.methodName(arguments).

questions.q: When calling a method on another object, such as minutes.increment(), the called method must be:
o: a public method in the class to which that object belongs
a method in the same class as the calling code
a private method in the class to which that object belongs
declared as static
questions.e: An external call can only reach a public method of the other object's class; if increment() had been private, it could not have been invoked from outside.

questions.q: From within a class's own code, which methods of that class can be invoked without an object name?
o: Public methods only
Both public and private methods
Private methods only
Neither, an object name is always required
questions.e: An internal call such as updateDisplay() reaches a method in the same class, and both public and private methods of one's own class can be invoked this way.

questions.q: From the perspective of a class's own code, the name of the object on which that code executes is always:
o: super
this
self
null
questions.e: The name of the object on which class code executes is always this, so an internal call may optionally be written this.updateDisplay().

questions.q: Which statement about null in Java is correct?
o: All object variables are initially zero and cannot be tested
A variable can be compared with null but never assigned null
null is a primitive value of type int
All object variables are initially null and can be tested against null
questions.e: null is a special Object in Java. All object variables, of any class, are initially null; variables can be tested to see whether they are null, and can also be assigned null, which loses the reference to whatever they held.

questions.q: What is the effect of assigning null to an object variable that currently refers to an object?
o: The assignment is rejected by the compiler
The object itself is immediately deleted from the source code
The variable becomes a primitive type
The reference to the previously held object is lost
questions.e: Variables can be assigned null, losing the reference to anything they were previously holding.

questions.q: Which pair correctly contrasts a primitive type variable with an object type variable?
o: Both hold references, but only object variables may be null
Both hold values directly, but only primitives may be null
A primitive variable holds a reference; an object variable holds a value directly
A primitive variable holds a value directly; an object variable holds a reference
questions.e: A primitive-type variable such as int i holds the value itself, while an object-type variable holds a reference to an object, which is why assignment behaves differently for the two.

questions.q: Which pair gives an application that needs a collection and the objects it groups?
o: A loop counter grouping its increments
A single calculator grouping its two operands
A constructor grouping its parameters
A library catalog grouping book or file records
questions.e: Applications that involve collections of objects include personal organizers (notes), library catalogs (files or books) and student-record systems (records). In each case the number of items stored varies as items are added and deleted.

questions.q: Defining one class with a separate field for each item to be stored has which drawback?
o: The class cannot have a constructor
The possible number of entries is fixed rather than variable
Fields cannot hold object references
The objects are not grouped at all
questions.e: Giving a class one field per item fixes the number of entries. The alternative of simply creating one object per item has a different drawback: the objects are not grouped at all, just living individually. Both point to the need for a collection.

questions.q: Java refers to its libraries of predefined useful classes as:
o: namespaces
assemblies
packages
modules
questions.e: Libraries are collections of a large number of predefined useful classes; Java calls its libraries packages.

questions.q: Which package contains the classes used for grouping objects, including ArrayList?
o: java.collections
java.util
java.lang
java.io
questions.e: The java.util package contains classes for grouping objects; ArrayList is one example of a collection class from it.

questions.q: Which statement correctly declares and creates a collection that holds String objects?
o: private ArrayList notes<String>; ... notes = new ArrayList();
private String<ArrayList> notes; ... notes = new String<ArrayList>();
private ArrayList<String> notes = ArrayList.new<String>();
private ArrayList<String> notes; ... notes = new ArrayList<String>();
questions.e: The field declares an ArrayList of String, and the constructor call new ArrayList<String>() creates it. That constructor needs no arguments.

questions.q: When using a collection, which two things must be specified?
o: The maximum capacity and the initial capacity
The package name and the constructor name
The type of collection and the type of objects it will contain
The index of the first element and the index of the last
questions.e: We specify the type of collection, for instance ArrayList, and the type of objects it will contain, for instance <String>, giving what is read aloud as 'ArrayList of String'.

questions.q: Which statement about the capacity of an ArrayList is correct?
o: It has no capacity limit because it stores no data
Its capacity must be set by calling size()
Its capacity is fixed when it is created
It increases its capacity as necessary
questions.e: A collection increases its capacity as necessary, so there are no memory problems of the kind a fixed-size structure would cause.

questions.q: How does a collection report how many objects it currently holds?
o: It recounts the elements each time add() is called
It cannot report its count; the client must track it
It keeps a private count, available through the size() accessor
It keeps a public count field that clients read directly
questions.e: The collection keeps a private count, which clients obtain using the size() accessor method.

questions.q: In what order does an ArrayList keep the objects stored in it?
o: The order in which they were added
An unspecified order that may change
Reverse order of insertion
Alphabetical order of their text form
questions.e: An ArrayList keeps the objects in the order they are added, which is why each item has a meaningful index.

questions.q: A method 'public void storeNote(String note) { notes.add(note); }' is an example of:
o: casting, since a String is converted to a note
overloading, since add and storeNote have the same purpose
delegation, since the work is passed on to the collection object
inheritance, since the method is inherited from ArrayList
questions.e: The class does not do the storing itself but passes the task on to its ArrayList field; the same pattern appears in 'return notes.size();' for counting.

questions.q: In a collection, index numbering is implicit and always starts from:
o: the collection's size
one
the first non-null element
zero
questions.e: Index numbering is implicit, always starting from zero, so a collection of three items has indices 0, 1 and 2.

questions.q: Which ArrayList method retrieves the object stored at a given index?
o: remove
get
size
add
questions.e: The main ArrayList methods are add, get, remove and size; get retrieves the element at the given index.

questions.q: Why does a showNote(int noteNumber) method check both that noteNumber is not negative and that it is less than numberOfNotes()?
o: Only the negative check is strictly needed; the second is redundant
Both checks guard against the collection being empty only
The checks convert the index into a valid one
Both checks are needed because only indices from 0 up to one less than the count are valid
questions.e: Valid indices run from zero up to one less than the number of items, so the method must reject negative values and values at or beyond the current count before calling get.

questions.q: After removing the item at index 1 from a collection of four items, what happens to the item that was at index 2?
o: It stays at index 2
It is also removed
It moves to index 1
It moves to index 3
questions.e: Removal affects numbering: the items after the removed one shift down by one position, so index values may change when items are removed or further items are added.

questions.q: Collection classes such as ArrayList are examples of:
o: parameterised or generic classes
interfaces
abstract classes
final classes
questions.e: Collection classes are parameterised, or generic, classes. ArrayList implements list functionality with methods such as add, get and size, and the type parameter says what kind of data the list should hold, as in ArrayList<Person> or ArrayList<TicketMachine>.

questions.q: What does the type parameter in ArrayList<Person> specify?
o: The maximum number of elements
The name of the variable holding the list
The kind of data the list is to hold
The package the list belongs to
questions.e: The <type> parameter says what kind of data we want the list to hold, for example ArrayList<Person> or ArrayList<TicketMachine>.

questions.q: In the statement 'String message = (String) notes.get(0);' the construct (String) is:
o: a cast, used to store the result of get into a variable of a specific type
a constructor call that creates a new String
a comment marking the expected type
a type parameter supplied to the collection
questions.e: Casting is used to store the result of get into a variable of a specific type. It is needed when the collection has no type parameter and so yields elements of type Object.

questions.q: Which statement about hiding the implementation details of a collection is correct?
o: Hiding the details prevents the collection from growing
The internal details must be understood before the collection can be used
Hiding the details makes the size() accessor unnecessary
Not knowing how it works internally does not prevent us from using it, and someone else has already done that work
questions.e: The details of how capacity growth, counting and ordering are achieved are hidden; the advantage is that someone else did the work and we need only know how to use the class.

questions.q: A personal notebook example requires that notes may be stored, individual notes can be viewed, how many are stored can be reported, and:
o: at most ten notes may be held
notes cannot be removed once added
notes are stored in alphabetical order
there is no limit to the number of notes
questions.e: The requirements are that notes may be stored, individual notes can be viewed, there is no limit to the number of notes, and the number currently stored can be reported.

questions.q: Iteration is defined as doing something several times where:
o: the number of times may vary due to circumstances
the number of times is fixed at compile time
the action never terminates
the action is performed exactly once per object
questions.e: Iteration means doing something several times, where the number of times may vary due to circumstances; most programming languages include loop statements to make this possible.

questions.q: How many sorts of loop statement does Java have?
o: Two
Four
Three
One
questions.e: Java has three sorts of loop statement.

questions.q: In a while loop that lists collection items, what does the statement index++ do?
o: Returns the item at position index
Increments index by one, equivalent to index += 1 or index = index + 1
Increments index by the collection's size
Resets index to zero
questions.e: index++ increments the variable by one and is equivalent to index += 1 and to index = index + 1.

questions.q: Which loop correctly lists every element of a collection called notes using an index?
o: int index = 0; while(index <= notes.size()) { System.out.println(notes.get(index)); index++; }
int index = 0; while(index < notes.size()) { System.out.println(notes.get(index)); index++; }
int index = 0; while(index < notes.size()) { System.out.println(notes.get(index)); }
int index = 1; while(index < notes.size()) { System.out.println(notes.get(index)); index++; }
questions.e: The index must start at zero, the test must use strictly less than the size, and the index must be incremented inside the loop; the other versions skip the first element, run past the end, or never terminate.

questions.q: How is an Iterator object obtained from a collection?
o: By casting the collection to Iterator
By calling the collection's Iterator() constructor
By calling the collection's next() method
By calling the collection's iterator() method
questions.e: Collections have an iterator() method, which returns an Iterator object. Note the difference in capitalisation between the Iterator type and the iterator() method.

questions.q: Which method of an Iterator reports whether any elements remain?
o: remove()
hasNext()
next()
size()
questions.e: hasNext() returns a boolean saying whether more elements remain; next() returns the next element. Note that some treatments count remove() as a third Iterator method while others list only next() and hasNext().

questions.q: Which import is required to use an Iterator by name?
o: import java.util.Iterator;
import java.io.Iterator;
import java.lang.Iterator;
import java.util.ArrayList;
questions.e: Iterator comes from the java.util package, the same package as ArrayList.

questions.q: Which loop correctly prints every element of a collection using an Iterator?
o: Iterator it = new Iterator(notes); while(it.hasNext()) { System.out.println(it.next()); }
Iterator it = notes.iterator(); while(it.hasNext()) { System.out.println(it.next()); }
Iterator it = notes.iterator(); while(it.next()) { System.out.println(it.hasNext()); }
Iterator it = notes.iterator(); for(it.hasNext()) { System.out.println(it.next()); }
questions.e: The iterator is obtained from the collection, hasNext() controls the loop, and next() both returns the current element and advances the iterator.

questions.q: Which way of iterating over a collection should be chosen when every element must be processed?
o: A for-each loop
An Iterator object, because it is always fastest
A do-while loop
A classical for loop with an index, in all cases
questions.e: A for-each loop is used when we want to process every element; a while loop or an Iterator object is used when we might want to stop part way through.

questions.q: Which way of iterating is required if elements are to be removed from the collection during the traversal?
o: A classical for loop
A nested while loop
An Iterator object
A for-each loop
questions.e: An Iterator is used when we might want to stop part way through, when indexed access is inefficient or impossible, and when removing from a collection.

questions.q: An Iterator is often preferred for collections in which:
o: elements are primitive values
the collection has fewer than ten elements
the number of elements is fixed
indexed access is not very efficient, or is impossible
questions.e: Iterator objects are often used with collections where indexed access is not very efficient, or impossible.

questions.q: Which loop statement should be used for repetition that does not involve a collection at all?
o: A for-each loop
No loop is possible
A while loop
An Iterator object
questions.e: A while loop is used when we might want to stop part way through, and for repetition that does not involve a collection.

questions.q: A fixed-size collection type offered by most programming languages is called:
o: a list
an array
a set
a map
questions.e: When the maximum collection size can be pre-determined, programming languages usually offer a special fixed-size collection type: an array.

questions.q: Which statement correctly contrasts Java arrays with collections?
o: Both can store primitives, but only arrays can store objects
Neither can store primitive-type values
Arrays can store objects or primitive-type values, whereas collections can store objects only
Collections can store objects or primitive-type values, whereas arrays can store objects only
questions.e: Java arrays can store objects or primitive-type values, while collections can store objects only. Arrays also use a special syntax, for historical reasons, and access to arrays is typically more efficient.

questions.q: Why do Java arrays use a special syntax rather than the method-call style used by collections?
o: For historical reasons
Because arrays are not objects in any sense
Because square brackets are faster to parse
Because arrays have no methods at all
questions.e: Arrays use a special syntax, different from the method concept, for historical reasons; access to arrays is also typically more efficient.

questions.q: Which statement creates an array object able to hold 24 int values?
o: hourCounts = new int[24];
hourCounts = new int(24);
hourCounts = int[24];
hourCounts = new array<int>(24);
questions.e: The general form is new type[integer-expression], so new int[24] creates the array object. The separate declaration private int[] hourCounts; declares the variable without creating an array.

questions.q: In 'private int[] hourCounts;' what has happened?
o: A collection of type int has been created
The array variable is declared but no array object has been created yet
An array of 24 elements has been created
An empty array of length zero has been created
questions.e: That line is an array variable declaration only; the array object is created separately by an expression such as new int[24].

questions.q: Array indices in Java always start at:
o: a value chosen by the programmer
zero
the array's length minus one
one
questions.e: Array indices always start at zero, and square-bracket notation such as hourCounts[hour] is used to access an element.

questions.q: Array elements may be used like ordinary variables. Which of these is therefore valid?
o: ++hourCounts(hour);
hourCounts[hour]++;
hourCounts++[hour];
hourCounts.increment(hour);
questions.e: Elements are used like ordinary variables, on the left of an assignment such as hourCounts[hour] = ...;, in expressions such as adjusted = hourCounts[hour] - 3;, and with increment operators such as hourCounts[hour]++;.

questions.q: Which for loop correctly iterates over every element of an array named hourCounts?
o: for(int hour = 1; hour <= hourCounts.length; hour++)
for(int hour = 0; hour <= hourCounts.length; hour++)
for(int hour = 0; hour < hourCounts.size(); hour++)
for(int hour = 0; hour < hourCounts.length; hour++)
questions.e: An array's extent is given by the length field, not a size() method, and because indices start at zero the test must be strictly less than length.

questions.q: How is the number of elements in a Java array obtained?
o: Through its length field
By calling its count() method
By calling its size() method
By calling its numberOfElements() method
questions.e: An array exposes length, as in hourCounts.length, while a collection such as ArrayList provides a size() method.

questions.q: A weblog-analyzer program examines web server access records to support which kinds of task?
o: Finding the most popular pages, busiest periods, data delivered and broken references
Designing the site's visual layout
Allocating server memory and tuning the kernel
Encrypting server traffic and managing certificates
questions.e: A web server records details of each access, and analysing those records supports the webmaster's tasks: most popular pages, busiest periods, how much data is being delivered, and broken references. One such analysis counts accesses by hour.

questions.q: In a web log whose line records hold year, month, day, hour and minute, what does the record '2011 11 15 10 55' represent?
o: The 11th of the 15th month of 2011 at 10:55
The 15th of November 2011 at 10:55
The 11th of November 2015 at 10:55
2011 accesses in 11 minutes on day 15
questions.e: The fields appear in the order year, month, day, hour, minute, so 2011 11 15 10 55 is 15 November 2011 at 10:55.

questions.q: An array is the appropriate choice of structure when:
o: the number of items will vary widely
a fixed-size collection is required
only object references will be stored
items must be removed frequently from the middle
questions.e: Arrays are appropriate where a fixed-size collection is required; they use special syntax and are classically traversed with a for loop.

questions.q: Which statement captures the 'change or die' view of software?
o: Software outlives its maintainers regardless of its structure
Software is either continuously maintained or it dies, because software that cannot be maintained will be thrown away
Software should be frozen after release to protect its quality
Software that is maintained too often becomes unreliable
questions.e: There are only two options for software: either it is continuously maintained, or it dies. Software that cannot be maintained will be thrown away.

questions.q: Unlike a novel, software is characteristically:
o: read far more often than it is modified, so structure hardly matters
extended, corrected, maintained, ported and adapted by different people over decades
evaluated only on whether it is correct at one moment
written once by one author and then left unchanged
questions.e: Software is extended, corrected, maintained, ported and adapted, and the work is done by different people over time, often decades. Quality of code therefore requires much more than performing correctly at one time.

questions.q: Which two concepts are the important criteria for assessing the quality of code?
o: Fan-in and leanness
Abstraction and encapsulation
Inheritance and polymorphism
Coupling and cohesion
questions.e: Two important concepts for assessing the quality of code are coupling and cohesion.

questions.q: Coupling refers to:
o: links between separate units of a program
the number and diversity of tasks a single unit is responsible for
the depth of an inheritance hierarchy
the amount of duplicated code in a class
questions.e: Coupling refers to links between separate units of a program; cohesion, by contrast, refers to the number and diversity of tasks a single unit is responsible for.

questions.q: Two classes that depend closely on many details of each other are said to be:
o: loosely cohesive
tightly coupled
highly cohesive
loosely coupled
questions.e: If two classes depend closely on many details of each other, they are tightly coupled; the goal is loose coupling.

questions.q: What does a class diagram provide with respect to coupling?
o: No information about coupling at all
An exact measurement of coupling
Limited hints at the degree of coupling
A measure of cohesion rather than coupling
questions.e: A class diagram provides limited hints at the degree of coupling between classes.

questions.q: Loose coupling makes which two things possible?
o: Removing all class diagrams, and eliminating the need for testing
Understanding one class without reading others, and changing one class with little or no effect on others
Sharing fields directly between classes, and skipping accessor methods
Reducing the number of classes, and merging unrelated responsibilities
questions.e: Loose coupling makes it possible to understand one class without reading others and to change one class with little or no effect on other classes; it therefore increases maintainability.

questions.q: Which consequence follows from tight coupling?
o: Maintainability increases because classes share knowledge
Changes to one class bring a cascade of changes to other classes
The flow of control between objects becomes trivially simple
Each class can be understood entirely in isolation
questions.e: With tight coupling, changes to one class bring a cascade of changes to other classes, classes are harder to understand in isolation, and the flow of control between objects of different classes is complex.

questions.q: Cohesion refers to:
o: the number of parameters a method takes
the number of subclasses a class has
the number and diversity of tasks that a single unit is responsible for
the links between separate units of a program
questions.e: Cohesion refers to the number and diversity of tasks that a single unit is responsible for. A unit responsible for one single logical task has high cohesion.

questions.q: A unit responsible for one single logical task is said to have:
o: tight coupling
high cohesion
low cohesion
loose coupling
questions.e: If each unit is responsible for one single logical task, we say it has high cohesion, and high cohesion is the goal.

questions.q: The term 'unit', when discussing cohesion, applies to:
o: classes only
classes, methods and modules (packages)
methods only
fields and parameters
questions.e: 'Unit' applies to classes, methods and modules, which in Java means packages.

questions.q: High cohesion makes which of the following easier?
o: Removing the need for a class diagram
Sharing implementation details between unrelated classes
Using descriptive names for variables, methods and classes
Writing longer methods with more responsibilities
questions.e: High cohesion makes it easier to understand what a class or method does, to use descriptive names for variables, methods and classes, and to reuse classes and methods.

questions.q: Which symptoms indicate loose cohesion?
o: Methods are short and classes represent a single entity
Methods perform multiple tasks and classes have no clear identity
Changes to one class cascade into many others
Classes depend on many details of each other
questions.e: Loosely cohesive classes and methods are to be avoided: methods perform multiple tasks and classes have no clear identity. Cascading changes across classes is a symptom of tight coupling instead.

questions.q: Applied at class level, cohesion means that classes should:
o: contain one single method
be responsible for one single line of code
have exactly one field
represent one single, well defined entity
questions.e: At class level, classes should represent one single, well defined entity; at method level, a method should be responsible for one and only one well defined task.

questions.q: Code duplication is a problem because it:
o: indicates bad design, makes maintenance harder, and can lead to errors during maintenance
always increases runtime performance
reduces the total size of the codebase
makes classes more cohesive
questions.e: Code duplication is an indicator of bad design, makes maintenance harder, and can lead to the introduction of errors during maintenance.

questions.q: Responsibility-driven design answers which question?
o: Where should a new method be added, that is, in which class
Which design notation should be used
How many fields a class should have
How long a project schedule should be
questions.e: Responsibility-driven design addresses where a new method should be added: each class should be responsible for manipulating its own data, and the class that owns the data should be responsible for processing it.

questions.q: The central rule of responsibility-driven design is that:
o: the class that uses the data most often should own it
data processing should be placed in the class with the fewest methods
the class that owns the data should be responsible for processing it
a single controller class should process all data
questions.e: Each class should be responsible for manipulating its own data; the class that owns the data should be responsible for processing it. Responsibility-driven design leads to low coupling.

questions.q: Responsibility-driven design leads to:
o: low cohesion
deeper inheritance hierarchies
low coupling
high coupling
questions.e: Responsibility-driven design leads to low coupling, because responsibilities are placed with the data they act on.

questions.q: Reducing coupling and applying responsibility-driven design both aim to:
o: localize change, so that as few classes as possible are affected
eliminate the need for future changes
centralize change, so that all edits happen in one controller class
distribute each change evenly across all classes
questions.e: One aim of reducing coupling and of responsibility-driven design is to localize change: when a change is needed, as few classes as possible should be affected.

questions.q: Why do classes and methods need periodic refactoring during maintenance?
o: Because code is added over time, so classes and methods tend to become longer
Because new programming languages are released
Because fields lose their types over time
Because compilers change their optimisation rules
questions.e: When classes are maintained, code is often added, and classes and methods tend to become longer; every now and then they should be refactored to maintain cohesion and low coupling.

questions.q: What is the correct discipline when refactoring code?
o: Do the refactoring alone without changing functionality, and test both before and after
Refactor after releasing the new functionality
Skip testing, since refactoring does not change behaviour
Combine refactoring with new features so that only one test cycle is needed
questions.e: Separate the refactoring from making other changes: first do the refactoring only, without changing the functionality, and test before and after refactoring to ensure nothing was broken.

questions.q: The questions 'how long should a class be?' and 'how long should a method be?' are answered in terms of:
o: lines of code and cyclomatic complexity
cohesion and coupling
fan-in and fan-out
inheritance depth and field count
questions.e: These common design questions can be answered in terms of cohesion and coupling rather than by fixed numeric limits.

questions.q: According to the design guidelines, a method is too long if it:
o: does more than one logical task
has more than three parameters
contains more than one return statement
exceeds fifty lines of code
questions.e: A method is too long if it does more than one logical task, and a class is too complex if it represents more than one logical entity. These are guidelines that still leave much open to the designer.

questions.q: According to the design guidelines, a class is too complex if it:
o: is referenced by more than five other classes
represents more than one logical entity
contains more than ten methods
has more than one constructor
questions.e: A class is too complex if it represents more than one logical entity; a method is too long if it does more than one logical task.

questions.q: An enumerated type in Java is introduced using which keyword in place of class?
o: constant
enumerate
final
enum
questions.e: An enumerated type is a language feature that uses enum instead of class to introduce a type name.

questions.q: The simplest use of an enumerated type is to:
o: define a set of significant names, as an alternative to static int constants
define a set of methods without bodies
define a collection with a fixed size
define a class that cannot be subclassed
questions.e: The simplest use of an enum is to define a set of significant names, serving as an alternative to static int constants when the constants' values would be arbitrary.

questions.q: Given 'public enum CommandWord { GO, QUIT, HELP, UNKNOWN; }', which statement is correct?
o: The names must be instantiated with new CommandWord()
The enum may not contain fields, constructors or methods
Each name represents an object of the enum type, referred to as CommandWord.HELP, and such objects are not created directly
Each name is an int constant that may be incremented
questions.e: Each name represents an object of the enum type, for example CommandWord.HELP; enum objects are not created directly, and enum definitions can also have fields, constructors and methods.

questions.q: In a text adventure game built from the classes Game, Room, Parser, Command and CommandWords, which class reads user input?
o: Game
CommandWords
Parser
Command
questions.e: Parser reads user input; Command represents a single user command, CommandWords holds the recognized user commands, Game is the starting point and main control loop, and Room represents a room in the game.

questions.q: In that same game, which class is the starting point and holds the main control loop?
o: Command
Room
Game
Parser
questions.e: Game is the starting point and main control loop. Room is a room in the game, Parser reads user input, Command is a user command, and CommandWords lists the recognized commands.

questions.q: Asking how much work is needed to add two new movement directions to an existing game is a practical way to test:
o: the number of classes in the program
the size of the compiled program
the execution speed of the program
the coupling and cohesion of the existing design
questions.e: Asking what must change, and how easily the changes can be applied thoroughly, exposes the quality of the design; a well-designed program localizes such a change.

questions.q: In a small social network application that stores both text posts and photo posts, what distinguishes the two kinds of post?
o: A text post holds a multi-line text message, while a photo post holds a photo and a caption
A text post has no author, while a photo post does
A text post holds a caption, while a photo post holds a multi-line message
A text post cannot be commented on, while a photo post can
questions.e: MessagePost holds a multi-line text message; PhotoPost holds a photo (a filename) and a caption. Both support operations such as search, display and remove.

questions.q: Two classes MessagePost and PhotoPost each declare the fields username, timestamp, likes and comments, plus their own extra fields. What design problem does this create?
o: An inability to create objects of either class
Loss of encapsulation of the shared fields
Code duplication, which makes maintenance difficult and risks bugs through incorrect maintenance
Excessive coupling between the two classes
questions.e: The two classes are very similar, with large parts identical. Code duplication makes maintenance difficult and more work, and introduces the danger of bugs through incorrect maintenance. The same duplication appears in the client class that holds the two collections.

questions.q: Which field initialisation records the moment a post was created?
o: timestamp = System.currentTimeMillis();
timestamp = System.time();
timestamp = new Date();
timestamp = 0;
questions.e: The constructor sets timestamp = System.currentTimeMillis(), alongside likes = 0 and the creation of an empty comments list.

questions.q: Which Java keyword establishes that one class inherits from another?
o: implements
super
extends
inherits
questions.e: A subclass is declared with extends, as in 'public class MessagePost extends Post'. The superclass declaration itself is unchanged. The keyword implements is used for interfaces instead.

questions.q: When inheritance is introduced, where should the fields username, timestamp, likes and comments be placed?
o: In each subclass separately, for clarity
In the client class that holds the collection
In an interface implemented by both subclasses
In the superclass Post, so both subclasses inherit them
questions.e: The superclass defines the common attributes via fields; the subclasses inherit those attributes and add other attributes of their own, such as message in MessagePost and filename and caption in PhotoPost.

questions.q: Which statement about superclass constructor calls is correct?
o: A subclass constructor may place the super call anywhere in its body
A subclass constructor must never call the superclass constructor
A subclass constructor must always contain a super call, and it must be the first statement
The super call is required only when the superclass has no fields
questions.e: Subclass constructors must always contain a 'super' call, and it must be the first statement in the subclass constructor.

questions.q: If a subclass constructor contains no explicit super call, what happens?
o: The subclass constructor is silently ignored
The compiler reports an error in every case
The superclass fields are left uninitialised but the code compiles
The compiler inserts one without parameters, which works only if the superclass has a parameterless constructor
questions.e: If no super call is written, the compiler inserts one without parameters; this works only if the superclass has a constructor without parameters.

questions.q: Replacing two collections, one of MessagePost and one of PhotoPost, with a single ArrayList<Post> has which effect on the client class?
o: It removes the code duplication there, leaving one field, one list creation, one add method and one loop
It forces the client to use casts on every element
It prevents the client from displaying posts
It requires the client to know about both subclasses
questions.e: Using the superclass type avoids code duplication in the client class: only one field, one ArrayList creation, one add method, and a single loop over the mixed collection are needed.

questions.q: Which benefits does inheritance provide?
o: Avoiding code duplication, code reuse, easier maintenance and extendibility
Automatic generation of test cases
Elimination of the need for constructors
Faster execution and smaller memory use
questions.e: Inheritance helps with avoiding code duplication, code reuse, easier maintenance and extendibility, and it simplifies the code.

questions.q: Classes define types; subclasses therefore define:
o: supertypes
subtypes
interfaces
instances
questions.e: Classes define types and subclasses define subtypes. Objects of subclasses can be used where objects of supertypes are required, which is called substitution.

questions.q: The principle that objects of subclasses can be used wherever objects of their supertype are required is called:
o: encapsulation
casting
substitution
overloading
questions.e: This is substitution: it is what allows a single addPost(Post post) method to accept both a MessagePost and a PhotoPost.

questions.q: Given classes Vehicle, Car and Bicycle where Car and Bicycle are subclasses of Vehicle, which assignments are legal?
o: Car c = new Vehicle(); and Bicycle b = new Vehicle();
Car c = new Bicycle();
Vehicle v = new Vehicle(); only
Vehicle v2 = new Car(); and Vehicle v3 = new Bicycle();
